hook: The $8.98 lights everyone skips before ribbon

scenes.visual_prompt: A fully ribboned and ornamented tree that still looks dim and flat despite the decorations
scenes.on_screen_text: Why does this tree look flat?
scenes.voiceover: I almost blamed the ribbon for this. It wasn't the ribbon.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up comparing a 50-bulb light strand (only covering outer tips) to a 100-bulb strand threaded into interior branches
scenes.voiceover: It was the lights. A 50-bulb strand only lights the outer third of the tree. These Minetom strands run 5 bulbs per foot, dense enough to reach the interior.

scenes.visual_prompt: Product shot of Minetom Clear Christmas String Lights box, 100 count, 20 feet, $8.98 price tag visible
scenes.voiceover: These run $8.98 for 100 count, 20 feet, and they're sitting at 4.6 stars across more than 8,500 ratings.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands threading a warm-white strand from trunk outward through multiple branch layers, 4-5 strands laid out
scenes.voiceover: For a 7.5-foot tree, that's 4 to 5 of these 20-foot strands threaded from the trunk outward, before a single piece of ribbon goes on.

scenes.visual_prompt: Side-by-side of cool-white LED vs warm-white incandescent light under velvet ribbon
scenes.voiceover: Warm-white specifically — cool-white LED makes velvet ribbon look flat instead of rich.

scenes.visual_prompt: Finished tree glowing warmly under full ribbon and ornament clusters
scenes.on_screen_text: You can't fix this layer after the fact
scenes.voiceover: This is the one layer you can't go back and fix without undoing everything you put on top of it.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card pointing to blog link
scenes.on_screen_text: Full light layer math on the blog

caption: Everyone skips this step because it's invisible once the tree is done — but it's the reason some trees look dim under all that ribbon. The light layer that has to go on first, and the exact strand count for a 7.5-foot tree.
